narrative.overview: A near-black studio surface gives visual work its cinematic setting. When the page presents engineering evidence, a cool, light document surface brings the result into focus. The composition remains spacious and typographic; dense interfaces are reserved for demonstrations.
keyCharacteristics: Large, plain-language headings in Geist Sans with generous surrounding space.
Dark charcoal surfaces, restrained cool-indigo controls, and a light evidence surface.
A wide reading grid for projects and experience; immersive motion in the creative sequence.
Strong visible focus states and readable static content when motion is reduced.

rules.name: The Evidence Contrast Rule
rules.body: Use the light surface for an output a visitor should inspect. Keep surrounding controls dark so the result has one clear focal point.

rules.name: The Result First Rule
rules.body: On constrained screens, the proof artifact appears before supporting source detail. Supporting context remains available through labelled controls.

dos: Do make the outcome the largest visual element inside a product demonstration.
Do label sample content and distinguish it from real operating status.
Do use concise project summaries before deeper architecture and proof.
Do preserve accessible text and navigation through every motion sequence.
donts: Don't make decorative concept art stand in for a product screenshot or benchmark.
Don't use the bright output treatment for every card; it marks an inspectable artifact.
Don't let long animation delay the first engineering evidence.
